note: Who ruled what c. 1650, for the overworld (build_overworld.py builds polygons from it) and the town files ('ruler'). GEOMETRY IS A PROXY: each polity is the union of modern administrative areas (OSM, extract_region.py -> admin.json) whose borders descend from the old ones, minus/plus the corrections listed. Good to a few km; where the 1650 line is known to differ, the difference is listed under 'deviations'. 'areas' entries are '<OSM name>|<admin_level>'. 'add'/'cut' are hand polygons [[lat, lon], ...].

polities.name: Hertogdom Brabant
polities.sovereign: Philip IV of Spain, as duke (Spanish Netherlands); governor Archduke Leopold Wilhelm 1647-56
areas: Région de Bruxelles-Capitale - Brussels Hoofdstedelijk Gewest|4
polities.addNote: Halen and its land (Brabant, a border fortress against Loon; inventory 140194) lies in today's province of Limburg; approximate square.
polities.deviations: The left bank of the Scheldt opposite Antwerp (Zwijndrecht, Burcht) is in today's province of Antwerp but belonged to the Land van Waas (Flanders) - not corrected. The Dutch forts Lillo and Liefkenshoek on the Scheldt are points of the Republic (see 'points'). Baarle-Hertog enclaves not modelled.
polities.source: nl.wikipedia 'Hertogdom Brabant'; Vrede van Munster (1648); inventory 140194 (Halen); docs/research/history-check.md F31 (governor)

polities.name: Heerlijkheid Mechelen
polities.sovereign: Philip IV of Spain, as lord of Mechelen (a separate province of the Spanish Netherlands, seat of the Great Council)
polities.deviations: Only the modern municipality of Mechelen; the lordship also held a few villages and the exclave of Heist-op-den-Berg (not modelled).

polities.name: Graafschap Vlaanderen
polities.sovereign: Philip IV of Spain, as count (Spanish Netherlands)
polities.deviations: Includes Imperial Flanders (Land van Aalst, east of the Scheldt up to the Dender) as part of Flanders. Bornem and the Waasland belong here. French conquests of the 1640s near the coast (Dunkirk, Bergues, Gravelines: French 1646-52 / 1644-) lie west of the region; Veurne's status in 1650 is NOT verified. Kortrijk had a French-built citadel (1646-48) but was Spanish again from 1648 (inventory 140006).

polities.name: Prinsbisdom Luik
polities.sovereign: Prince-bishop Ferdinand of Bavaria (1612-50), then Maximilian Henry of Bavaria (elected 1650); neutral in the Franco-Spanish war (neutrality recognised by Spain only in 1654, see history-check F76)

subdivisions.name: Graafschap Loon
subdivisions.note: Today's Belgian Limburg except Tongeren's quarter and the Maas lands; joined to Liège in 1366. Hasselt, Herk-de-Stad, Beringen, Bilzen, Borgloon, Maaseik, Bree, Peer, Hamont, Stokkem.
subdivisions.source: inventory 140046 (Borgloon: county ceased in 1366); nl.wikipedia 'Graafschap Loon'

subdivisions.name: Haspengouw / Luik
subdivisions.note: Tongeren and Sint-Truiden were good towns of the prince-bishopric itself (Sint-Truiden under the abbot and the prince-bishop jointly, inventory 140054).

polities.deviations: Halen (Brabant) is cut out. Voeren (Dalhem, Overmaas lands, disputed between Spain and the Republic until 1661) is in today's Limburg and is NOT cut out. Several small Loon enclaves and Brabant villages along the Demer line east of Diest are not modelled: the border runs a few km east of Diest (Webbekom and Molenstede Brabant, Lummen Loon) only approximately.

polities.name: Staats-Vlaanderen
polities.sovereign: States General of the Dutch Republic (Generality Land; west part administered with Zeeland), confirmed by the Peace of Münster 1648
polities.deviations: Zeeland cut at the Westerschelde midline. Includes the drowned land of Saeftinghe (Hulster Ambacht, in States hands since Hulst fell in 1645). The 1650 coastline of Zeeuws-Vlaanderen had more inlets (Braakman, Zwin) than today.

polities.name: Staats-Brabant
polities.sovereign: States General of the Dutch Republic (Generality Land: Bergen op Zoom, Breda, the Meierij of 's-Hertogenbosch), ceded by Spain at Münster 1648

polities.name: Maasland (Opper-Gelre, Overmaas, rijksgebieden)
polities.en: Lands on the Maas (Spanish Upper Guelders, the Overmaas lands, imperial abbeys)
polities.sovereign: mixed and partly disputed: Spanish Upper Guelders (Roermond, Venlo, Stevensweert), imperial abbey of Thorn, Jülich (Sittard), the Overmaas lands disputed until the partition of 1661, Maastricht a condominium of the Republic and Liège

polities.name: Graafschap Henegouwen
polities.sovereign: Philip IV of Spain, as count

polities.name: Graafschap Namen
polities.sovereign: Philip IV of Spain, as count

points.name: Fort Lillo
points.note: Dutch fort on the right bank of the Scheldt (built 1579-83, in States hands from 1585 until 1785); with Liefkenshoek it closed the river to Antwerp.

points.name: Fort Liefkenshoek
points.note: Dutch fort on the left bank opposite Lillo (1579-80; States from 1585 to 1785).

points.name: Fort Frederik-Hendrik / Kruisschans
points.note: Spanish counter-forts below Antwerp (Kruisschans, Sint-Filips, Sint-Marie) faced the Dutch forts; exact 1650 set not verified.

points.name: Fort Saeftinghe
points.note: States fort at the edge of the drowned land; position approximate.

diest.note: Barony of the House of Orange-Nassau within Spanish Brabant

antwerpen.note: Margraviate of Antwerp within Brabant; Spanish garrison in the citadel

sinttruiden.land: Prinsbisdom Luik; joint lordship of the abbot of Sint-Truiden and the prince-bishop (inventory 140054)

brussel.note: capital of the Spanish Netherlands; court of the governor

kortrijk.note: retaken by Spain in 1648 after French occupation 1646-48

ieper.note: taken by the French in 1648 and retaken by Spain in 1649 (not verified from a primary source)

turnhout.note: lordship given to Amalia van Solms (widow of Frederick Henry of Orange) in 1648, under Spanish sovereignty (inventory 300598)
